newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS- Merita H1 profit almost triples.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS- Merita H1 profit almost triples.

text.p: Merita Oy, Finland's largest banking group, on Wednesday said rallying stock markets and falling bad debts had helped produce a surge in first-half profit, enabling it to meet its full-year targets by June.

Reporting operating profit after credit losses at 1.81 billion markka ($324.8 million) against 681 million in the year-ago period, Merita said net loan and guarantee losses were slashed to 325 million from 824 million.
"We have achieved the target for the full year already in the first half and see a good development in the second half," a Merita spokeswoman told Reuters.
Merita's H1 income on securities trading ballooned to 1.35 billion markka net of hedging, up from 552 million.

The result was just over the top of the range of analysts' forecasts in a Reuters poll and several said they would hike full-year forecasts to add in between 300 and 350 million markka in unforeseen profit gleaned from the first half.
A 10-analyst poll before the report had a median full-year profit expectation for the group around 2.3 billion markka.
Merita had already said it expected full-year earnings to be distinctly better than in 1996, when it posted a 1.20 billion markka profit on ordinary operations.
"I see it quite positively also when we are speaking about '98," CEO Vesa Vainio told Reuters Financial Television.

But Merita's stock dipped 0.30 markka to 22.40 by 1210 GMT, hindered both by recent sharp gains and negative broad sentiment on stock markets internationally. Analysts were also waiting for more comments from the company later in the day.
"I think it was a remarkable achievement," said Henry Kallio at Aktia Securities: the result was well above his expectations.

A sharp fall in loan losses in the second quarter impressed both him and Ian McEwen at Lehman Brothers in London: down to only 50 million markka, they made up 0.36 percent of Merita's total lending portfolio in Q2.
Kallio said the normal level is about 0.8-0.9 percent. The company believes the full-year level could fall to 0.5 percent.
One analyst, requesting anonymity, said he expected to set a new 12-month target for the stock around 28 markka.

James Alexander at Kleinwort Benson in London said only underlying profit was a slight disappointment, with costs falling less sharply than he had hoped. He expected to maintain his recommendation on the stock at long-term "buy".
Merita's cost-revenue ratio at 1.73 was clearly up on H1 1996, but below typical levels of over 2.00 at neighbouring Swedish banks.
Vainio repeated that Merita aimed to pay dividends "which will increase in line with profit", but declined to elaborate.
Asked if Merita planned to go to the market to boost its capital position, he said: "We have no plans to raise capital from the market at the moment." ($ = 5.571 Finnish Markka)
